newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turk Cypriots suspend checkpoint curbs.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cypriots suspend checkpoint curbs.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot authorities on Thursday suspended restrictions on their side of the "green line" dividing the capital imposed the day before on Greek Cypriots living in the north of the divided island.
"As a sign of goodwill the Turkish Cypriot side has taken this decision," said Aytug Plumer, undersecretary for foreign affairs and defence of the breakaway state in northern Cyprus.
Plumer told Reuters Turkish Cypriot officials would review their position on checkpoint crossings on Monday.

The Turkish Cypriot administration had banned Greek Cypriots and members of the Maronite community from crossing on Wednesday in response to three straight weekends of protests by Greek Cypriots at the checkpoint to discourage tourist visits to the northern part of the island, occupied by Turkey since 1974.
Waldemar Rokoszewski, spokesman for the U.N. peacekeeping force in Cyprus, earlier said the situation at the checkpoint had returned to normal.
"Maronites were allowed to cross today and Greek Cypriots will be granted permission to travel on Friday," he told Reuters.

The closure had sparked an angry reaction from the Cypriot government, which controls the majority Greek Cypriot populated south, but appeared to strengthen the resolve of organisers to step up their protests.
"We will be there every day...We will start at the weekend and onwards," Greek Cypriot MP Marios Matsakis, who started the protests, told Reuters. "It will be even stronger."
Plumer said they expected the Greek Cypriots to "respond to the goodwill and lift their restrictions."
"However, the news coming from the other side is not good," he said, referring to comments made earlier by Matsakis.

Some 500 Greek Cypriots live in the Karpasia peninsula and 187 Maronites, who belong to a branch of the Roman Catholic church in the Middle East, live at a village on the north western coast of the island.

Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded and occupied its northern third in 1974 following a short-lived coup in Nicosia engineered by the military ruling Greece. The breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in the north is recognised only by Turkey.
United Nations officials have complained to the Cypriot government about the demonstrations, which effectively put a stop to all weekend visits by tourists to the island's north.
